subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Future of Tea
description: A fast breakdown of The Future of Tea for builders.

hook.text: Global tea consumption grows 5% per year. By 2027, the market will pass $80 billion.

buildup.text: Ready-to-drink bottled tea is the fastest-growing segment, driven by health-conscious consumers.

discovery.text: Functional teas—with added adaptogens, CBD, or probiotics—blur the line between beverage and supplement.

twist.text: Meanwhile, traditional tea ceremonies are gaining popularity as an antidote to digital overload.

climax.text: Tea's future is split: mass convenience on one side, mindful craftwork on the other. Both are thriving.

punchline.text: Five thousand years old and still evolving. That's tea.

quiz.question: What is the fastest-growing segment in the tea market?

details.summary: Tea faces challenges from climate change, labor issues, and competition from coffee and wellness drinks. But it also has enormous opportunities in health-conscious markets, premiumization, and the untapped potential of Western consumers discovering quality loose-leaf tea.
details.whyItMatters: Tea is the world's most consumed beverage after water. Its future affects billions of people, from growers to consumers, across every continent.
takeaways: Climate change and labor issues threaten tea's supply chain
Health trends and premiumization are driving new demand
Western markets are discovering quality tea as coffee did

faq.question: Is tea consumption growing or declining globally?
faq.answer: Global tea consumption is growing, driven by Asia and health-conscious Western consumers. Traditional markets like Britain are stable. Growth areas include specialty tea, ready-to-drink bottled tea, and matcha. The market is projected to reach over 300 billion dollars by 2030.

faq.question: Will the specialty tea movement grow like specialty coffee?
faq.answer: It has potential but faces barriers. Tea lacks coffee's cafe culture infrastructure in the West. Education about quality tea is less advanced among Western consumers. However, the health angle, variety of types, and ceremonial appeal give tea strong growth potential in the premium segment.
